title: Entry Key Registry
description: Schema for the generated entry_key_registry.json produced by 'specdev registry-generate'.

$schema.description: Schema URI identifying this document as an entry-key registry. Must be 'vc:entry-key-registry'.

_format_version.description: Semver string for the registry format.

_note.description: Human-readable note about the registry's origin. Consumers should not parse this string.

registry.description: Map of spec file key to entry-array metadata. A key is a spec file basename (e.g. '04_fr_list.json') or, for node kinds declared with x-node files, a relative glob (e.g. 'impl_context/ms_*_plan.json').

_sentinels.description: Top-level array names (e.g. 'canonical_refs_used') that appear in multiple spec files and are always corpus-excluded. These are NOT listed per-file in the registry.

steps_without_entry_arrays.description: Steps that register no node kind of their own: no schema file, or their records are blocks inside another step's file.

external_kinds.description: Kinds whose ids do not come from a step schema collection (today only 'seed', declared in the host's common/seed_manifest.json). Not listed in extraction_paths.json: these are not step files.

step.description: Step ID matching an entry in step_order.json::steps[], e.g. '04' or '16a'; or 'extras' for the entries of a record host (a non-step schema whose x-node sets files).

arrays.description: Entry-bearing arrays (or map-keyed collections) in the spec file.

array_path.description: jq-style path to the collection. '.name' descends an object property, '[]' follows an array property, '{}' follows a map property whose keys are the node ids. Examples: '.functional_requirements', '.milestones[].tasks', '.plan.items', '.environments{}'.

id_field.description: Name of the property that carries the entry's unique ID, e.g. 'fr_id' or 'id'. Absent on map-keyed entries, whose map key is the id.

kind.description: Logical kind of the entry, kebab-case, e.g. 'fr' or 'deliverable'.

nested.description: Nested entry-bearing arrays within each item of this array. IMPORTANT: the `array_path` for each nested entry is relative to each item of the parent array, NOT relative to the root spec document. To compute the full jq filter, concatenate: `<parent.array_path>[]<this.array_path>` (the leading `.` of the nested `array_path` is retained). For example, given `arrays[*].array_path = ".milestones"` and `nested[*].array_path = ".deliverables"`, the full jq path is `.milestones[].deliverables`.

corpus_excluded.description: When true, this array does not contribute to the nearest-id corpus. Exclusion is by the top key of the path: every entry under that top key is excluded. Only emitted when true.

source.description: Present only on entries derived from an x-node annotation.

role.description: Node role declared by x-node (annotation-derived entries only).

contract.description: Contract property names declared by x-node.

map_keyed.description: True when the collection is a map and the map key is the node id.

links.description: x-link declarations on the item, so one file holds what the link resolver reads.

field.description: Link field name (a verb of vc:core:graph#linkVerb).

required.description: True when every item must carry at least one value for this link.

built.description: True when the link counts toward the built computation. Default false.

same_step_kinds.description: Subset of kinds that may be held in the same step as the source.

additional_kinds.description: Subset of kinds that the field accepts in addition to the others; present only when the link declares it.

kind.description: The external kind name, kebab-case (today only 'seed').

source_file.description: Spec-relative file holding the ids, e.g. 'common/seed_manifest.json'.

array_path.description: Path of the id-bearing array inside source_file, e.g. '.seeds'.

id_field.description: Name of the property that carries each id.

top_of_graph.description: Always true: external kinds sit at the top of the graph and have no role.

rationale.description: Human-readable explanation for why this step has no or deferred entry arrays.
